title: Beyond win and lose
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Does every deal need a loser?
Jose said that you think of football and baseball: one team won, one team lost, and everything is win or lose. Come on, you have to win. He said that is one view of culture.
He said that some traditions, such as merchants who travelled from town to town, relied on long relationships, so both sides had to do well.

A student described a salesperson who is under pressure for his own job and then passes the confrontation to the customer, who is then also confrontational, although he does not have to answer emotionally.
Jose said that you have to gauge: if they call my bluff, what then? He said he did not have other cards.
A student said that he started to leverage a legal situation, saying: I am trying to get to an amicable solution, and then asked what could be done together.
Jose said that keeping true to those promises gives you more clients and more credibility: it goes round and round.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write a deal where you wanted to win.
Write what the other side wanted.
Write a way both could do well.
Write the leverage you actually have.
Write a promise you will keep.

check.q: What did Jose say culture often treats everything as?
What did a student say a pressured salesperson does?
What did Jose say keeping promises gives?

recap: Look past win or lose. Keep your promises.
